pr_title: 🐛 Fix CUDA for old GPUs without FP16 support
pr_body:
Fixes #21461

~This is a build-time solution that reflects https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.10.0/modules/dnn/src/cuda4dnn/init.hpp#L68-L82.~
~We shouldn't add an invalid target while building with `CUDA_ARCH_BIN` < 53.~
_(please see [this discussion](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/25880#discussion_r1668074505))_

This is a run-time solution that basically reverts [these lines](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/commit/d0fe6ad10967fd2b007a4cf83b00d6f8446deb42#diff-757c5ab6ddf2f99cdd09f851e3cf17abff203aff4107d908c7ad3d0466f39604L245-R245).

I've debugged these changes, [coupled with other fixes](https://github.com/gentoo/gentoo/pull/37479), on [Gentoo Linux](https://www.gentoo.org/) and [related tests passed](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16135391/opencv-4.10.0.20240708-224733.log.gz) on my laptop with `GeForce GTX 960M`.

Alternative solution:
  - #21462

_Best regards!_

issue_context.title: Do not report for FP16 compatibility on old Nvidia cards
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4801526f354057fecde2d70a52c69974aa5ee53f/modules/dnn/src/dnn.cpp#L251-L255

Since commit d0fe6ad10967fd2b007a4cf83b00d6f8446deb42 `cv::dnn::getAvailableBackends()` will list CUDA_FP16 for all Cuda devices even the old ones that do not have `__half` compute capabilities
The simple check has been removed, and I would suggest to add it back, what do you think @YashasSamaga ?
comments:
The check was removed as it was a bug. See this review comment: https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/19222/files#r588883516

I think the checks must be done every time in `getAvailableTargets` function instead of caching the results.

@YashasSamaga OK I understand the potential issue with multiple GPUs, however there's now other bugs because on my GTX 970, testing all available backends I get:
`
[ WARN:0] global D:\Dev\opencv\modules\dnn\src\dnn.cpp (2699) cv::dnn::dnn4_v20211004::Net::Impl::initCUDABackend The selected CUDA device does not support FP16 target; switching to FP32 target.
OpenCV: terminate handler is called! The last OpenCV error is:
OpenCV(4.5.4-dev) Error: Gpu API call (cuDNN did not return a suitable algorithm for convolution.) in cv::dnn::cuda4dnn::csl::cudnn::ConvolutionAlgorithm<struct __half>::ConvolutionAlgorithm, file D:\Dev\opencv\modules\dnn\src\cuda4dnn\csl\cudnn/convolution.hpp, line 303
`

Can you share a reproducer for this?

The FP16 check is done before initialization. The warning says that it switched target to FP32 but then the exception has `struct __half` in it. It shouldn't have been initializing FP16 operations in FP32 target.
I don't anything in an online repository but can share a small msvc project with you by email if it's fine

> What happens when calling setPreferableTarget(TARGET_CUDA_FP16) manually, is it handled?

It sets the internal preferred target variable to `DNN_TARGET_CUDA_FP16` and then clears the network state if the new target differs from the current target. This also implies a complete reinitialization in the next forward pass. In the first forward pass,`initCUDABackend` is called for initialization and this will check that FP16 isn't supported by the device and then switch to FP32 and continue with the initialization.

> `setDevice(conf.second)`

What is your intent for this line?

> Selecting the Nvidia card

Then your code isn't doing what you want. The target IDs are some internal constants in the DNN module. I think you're picking a random device with `setDevice(target)`. And CUDA target numbers are constants like 5 or 6. So I suspect that `setDevice` call always fails unless you have that many GPUs or remapped device IDs.

I think you read my code snippet too fast. `setDevice` takes the target as input because it also handles setting the device for OpenCL or OpenVino backend (extra code that I did not paste here). I'm not using the enum Target value in place of cuda device integer.

Regarding the bug, don't you think `initBackend` (and your on-the-fly target correction) is called too late for that?
https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4801526f354057fecde2d70a52c69974aa5ee53f/modules/dnn/src/dnn.cpp#L1498-L1504

_Hello @JulienMaille and @YashasSamaga,_

Would you mind reviewing an alternative fix for this issue?
  - #25880

_Thanks in advance!_
@Jamim thanks for the ping. however I must admit I don't understand why you suggest a _build time_ solution for something that happens at _runtime_!?

> @JulienMaille
> why you suggest a _build time_ solution for something that happens at _runtime_!?

That's a good question!

When we set `CUDA_ARCH_BIN` on build time, based on its value, we exactly know if `FP16` is supported or not on the _target_ architecture.
As I understand, there's no reason [to add](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/pull/25880/files#diff-afa733c13dfcdf15a40ac4f53faabe82d1417f8dc312542e6707160259997f68R125) the `DNN_BACKEND_CUDA, DNN_TARGET_CUDA_FP16` pair to the `backends` for `CUDA_ARCH_BIN` < 53, right?

I'm new to OpenCV internals, so if you see any downsides of this approach, please share your thoughts!

_Thanks!_
Uh that's right. Thanks for pointing this out. Well I'll look at the commit again and share feedback. However I won't be able to test it, I sold my GTX970 last year

review_comments:
Taking into account that the `version` is an integer variable, I think it would be a bit cleaner if we use `> 52` for this check.

```suggestion
        return (version > 52);
```
I prefer to stay with 53. It's well known constant in CUDA world. Also it's easier to "grep".
